title: Sum of Primes Between Number and Its Reverse
summary: Given an integer n, find the sum of all prime numbers between the lesser of n and its digit-reversed form r, and the greater of n and r, inclusive.
statement: Given an integer n, find the sum of all prime numbers between the lesser of n and its digit-reversed form r, and the greater of n and r, inclusive.
constraints: Reverse the decimal digits of positive n, dropping leading zeros created by reversal.
Use the inclusive interval between n and that reversed value.
Return the sum of all primes in the interval.
hints: Reverse n through its decimal text.
Test every value in the closed interval for primality.
A candidate is prime when it is at least two and has no divisor through its square root.
Summing exactly the passing candidates implements the definition independently of interval direction.
editorial: Summing exactly the passing candidates implements the definition independently of interval direction.

tests.explanation: The interval 13 through 31 contains primes summing to 132.
The reverse is two; primes from two through twenty sum to 77.
